digest.en: Xi used APEC to frame China as Asia’s open door while the US retreats. Jensen Huang faces Congress over national security risks, a sharp contrast to Beijing’s diplomatic push.
digest.hi: Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia employees in a 277-word message. Meanwhile, India and the Philippines signed cultural agreements covering lost wax sculptures.

articles.title: Xi’s APEC speech casts China as Asia’s open door as US closes
articles.summary: Xi Jinping addressed the APEC summit in Shenzhen, positioning China as an open alternative to US trade restrictions. He targeted Southeast Asian leaders and multinational executives, contrasting Washington's tariff deals and semiconductor controls with Beijing's stability. The speech aimed to secure economic partnerships without directly naming the United States. Taking the podium first at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping responded to Washington’s transactional tariff deals, revived Quad security alignment and tightening semiconductor controls with a calculated counter-pitch aimed squarely at wavering Southeast Asian capitals and multinational executives.

articles.title: Optics Over Substance Expected At Trump-Xi-Putin Summit
articles.summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin are scheduled to meet on the sidelines of the APEC conference in Shenzhen. Analysts expect the trilateral summit to prioritize optics over substantive policy outcomes. The gathering carries significant symbolic weight but is unlikely to produce major diplomatic breakthroughs or concrete agreements. A first-ever trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin to be held on the sidelines of this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference in Shenzhen may underwhelm despite its eyebrow-raising symbolism.

articles.title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
articles.summary: A survey of 195 organizations across 68 countries reveals that diversified funding strategies failed to protect civil society groups from the global aid retreat. The crisis extends beyond immediate financial shortfalls, indicating deeper structural vulnerabilities. Organizations that spent years building varied revenue streams are still facing severe operational challenges and instability. A survey of 195 organisations across more than 68 countries shows how the global aid retreat is hitting organizations that spent years building diverse funding streams.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank leak reveals nearly $600M in Epstein payments
articles.summary: Whistleblowers released over 15 million internal Deutsche Bank documents revealing nearly $600 million in payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein. Financial Times reporter Dan McCrum described the findings as exposing systemic failures and incompetence within the institution. The leak highlights significant compliance gaps and questionable conduct by the German bank regarding its client relationships. articles.title: Tit-For-Tat US-Iran Attacks Persist As Peace Deal Remains Elusive
articles.summary: US and Iranian forces exchanged air strikes across the Middle East. Gulf nations warned residents about incoming projectiles. Regional mediators attempted to halt the conflict. The low-level fighting continued despite diplomatic efforts to secure a peace deal. US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators.

articles.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
articles.summary: St Kitts and Nevis will end its citizenship-by-investment program. The decision follows European Union threats to revoke visa-free access for its citizens. Nevis premier Terrance Drew warned the move threatens the island economy and its ability to support vulnerable residents. St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free accessThe decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned. articles.title: Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life
articles.summary: About twenty Awá people emerged from voluntary isolation in Brazil’s Amazon. They made contact with villagers and accepted food to take back to their territory. Survival International reported the event, raising alarms about increased invasions into the group’s protected lands. articles.title: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody
articles.summary: An eight-year-old Haitian boy returned to his family in California. He was detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November. Agents placed him in restraints before transferring him to a facility in Texas. Representative Juan Vargas shared photos of the reunion. Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to TexasAn eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California. Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social.

articles.title: Ukrainian Defense Minister On Crimea Bridge Strike: 'We're Just Getting Started'
articles.summary: Ukraine struck the Crimean bridge, severing the peninsula's only direct road and rail link to the mainland. The attack occurred overnight on November 17. Russia retaliated by damaging two key bridges in Kyiv. Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov stated the campaign is just beginning. Ukraine has released video of its overnight strikes that damaged the bridge between the mainland and Russian-occupied Crimea, the only direct road and rail link to the peninsula.

articles.title: Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on ‘potential breach of national security’
articles.summary: Jensen Huang will testify before Congress on 1 December regarding national security concerns. His resignation followed an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will also appear. The hearing addresses the fallout from his departure and potential security breaches. High-stakes hearing comes in wake of resignation from Nvidia after alleged affair with suspected Chinese spyNvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang will testify before several congressional committees on 1 December, setting the stage for a high-stakes hearing in the wake of his resignation following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, has also agreed to appear for.

articles.title: How the news scramble is messing with Bank of Japan policymaking
articles.summary: Japan’s fragmented media environment complicates Bank of Japan policymaking. Shared cultural touchpoints have eroded over three decades. Policymakers now struggle to gauge public sentiment accurately. This shift impacts how the central bank communicates and anticipates market reactions to its decisions. For the past three decades, Japanese society still enjoyed something close to a shared media life. Major newspapers had enormous circulation.

articles.title: Trump turns brief Manila stop into pre-Shenzhen leverage haul
articles.summary: Trump used his brief Manila stop to secure leverage before heading to Shenzhen. He arrived after the ASEAN plenary had already concluded. The compressed schedule was initially viewed as a diplomatic slight. He leveraged the visit to negotiate terms ahead of his China meeting. When US President Donald Trump touched down in Manila on Tuesday afternoon (November 17), arriving only after the Association of Southeast Asian Nations had already concluded its formal plenary and handed its rotating chair to Singapore, early international coverage largely framed the compressed 24 hour visit as a diplomatic slight.

articles.title: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
articles.summary: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine reported that 2026 civilian casualties already exceed all previous years since the February 2022 invasion. The toll has risen dramatically compared to prior periods. This marks the highest recorded civilian death rate of the conflict to date. This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Ebola cases double in DR Congo, chemical exposure starts before birth, Türk concern over EU-Rwanda
articles.summary: The World Health Organization reported that Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have more than doubled in three months. Over 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths are now confirmed. The outbreak spans 67 health zones across eight provinces. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has more than doubled in three months, with more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths now reported in 67 health zones across eight provinces, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
articles.summary: Scientists and Indigenous communities presented new conservation tools at COP31 on Tuesday. Funding gaps and disagreements over fossil fuels continue to stall progress. Ministers are struggling to bridge these divisions. The gap between innovation and implementation remains wide. From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday.

articles.title: Hi-tech Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit
articles.summary: Xi Jinping used the APEC summit in Shenzhen to project China’s technological confidence. The host city displayed its skyline and advanced infrastructure to global leaders. This event signaled Beijing’s intent to position itself as a central economic power. The summit highlighted China’s growing influence in the region. articles.title: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact
articles.summary: Hundreds were arrested in Manila during anti-Trump protests. Demonstrations were fueled by anger over the Iran war and a new AI pact. Organizers expect up to 10,000 people to join the next round. Trump is arriving for the Asean summit. articles.title: Singapore’s AI balancing act exposes ASEAN’s split-stack dilemma
articles.summary: Singapore signed the San Francisco Declaration on secure AI foundations on November 15. This move highlights the difficulty of balancing US and Chinese tech ties. Southeast Asian nations face a split-stack dilemma. They must maintain access to American computing while keeping commercial links with China. Singapore’s diplomatic maneuvers in Manila this week illustrate the increasingly difficult technology-balancing act facing Southeast Asia: maintaining access to American advanced computing infrastructure while preserving commercial engagement with China.

articles.title: China’s J-10C missile upgrade could become a Taiwan war trap
articles.summary: China's J-10C fighters now carry short-range air-to-surface missiles. This creates a tactical risk if Taiwan's air defenses survive initial strikes. Jets forced closer to target face higher loss rates. The vulnerability mirrors US experiences in Iran. China’s integration of upgraded short-range air-to-surface missiles onto its frontline fighters exposes a critical vulnerability in a Taiwan conflict: if Taiwan’s air defenses survive initial barrages and exhaust China’s long-range stockpiles, jets forced closer with shorter-range weapons risk severe losses, mirroring US experience in Iran.

articles.title: Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen with little left to trade
articles.summary: Trump and Xi met in Shenzhen for the APEC summit. Technology policy is now a fixed national security arena, not a bargaining chip. Neither leader has significant concessions to offer. The meeting highlighted the rigid structure of current US-China relations. The November 18-19 APEC summit will reveal a fundamental shift in US-China relations: technology policy is no longer a flexible instrument of presidential bargaining, but an increasingly institutionalized arena of national security competition.

articles.title: Iranian Top Cleric Visits Bosnia As Tehran Seeks Opening To Europe
articles.summary: A senior Iranian cleric who briefly assumed supreme leader powers after Khamenei's death visited Sarajevo. He urged European nations to distance themselves from US and Israeli policies toward Tehran. The visit highlights Tehran's effort to cultivate a European diplomatic connection. A senior Iranian cleric who briefly helped exercise the powers of Iran's supreme leader following the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has visited Sarajevo, urging European countries to distance themselves from US and Israeli policies toward Tehran.

articles.title: With Soaring Prices And Police Crackdowns, Free Time Now Costs Too Much For Tehran's Youth
articles.summary: Tehran's youth face rising costs and police crackdowns on cafes and street gatherings. The economy remains battered by war and fears of renewed fighting. These pressures make socializing increasingly difficult for young people in the capital. With an economy battered by war and fears of renewed fighting, life in Iran’s capital keeps getting tighter. Add a crackdown on the cafes and street gatherings where young people socialize, and Tehran feels like it’s closing in on its youth.

articles.title: Progress ‘real’ but fragile, as remnants of war wreck young lives
articles.summary: Syria shows undeniable signs of progress two years after the Assad regime fell. Senior UN officials warn that explosive ordnance and winter threaten these gains. Severe funding shortfalls also complicate recovery efforts for young lives. Syria is showing “undeniable signs of progress” nearly two years after the fall of the Assad regime, but explosive ordnance, the approaching winter and severe funding shortfalls threaten those fragile gains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Monday.

articles.title: At his final ASEAN Summit, Guterres upholds cooperation and action on Myanmar
articles.summary: António Guterres urged stronger cooperation with ASEAN and an end to the Myanmar crisis during his final summit in Manila. The UN Secretary-General addressed regional leaders on Monday, emphasizing the need for collective action to resolve the ongoing humanitarian and political situation in Southeast Asia. UN Secretary-General António Guterres underscored the need for stronger collaboration with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and an end to the crisis in Myanmar, in remarks to regional leaders meeting in the Philippine capital Manila on Monday.

articles.title: COP31 enters decisive week as climate talks face political test and AI initiatives gather pace
articles.summary: COP31 enters its decisive week with new AI and green industrialization initiatives. Negotiators remain deadlocked on finance, fossil fuels, and adaptation. The UN talks face a significant political test in their final stretch. New international initiatives on artificial intelligence and green industrialization showcased technology’s growing role in climate action, even as negotiators remained deadlocked on finance, fossil fuels and adaptation ahead of the final stretch of the UN talks.

articles.title: अमेरिकी खुफिया एजेंसी CIA के हेडऑफिस में आग? अफरा-तफरी में पहुंची दमकल टीम, आसमान में दिखा काला धुआं
articles.summary: वर्जीनिया के लैंगली में सीआईए मुख्यालय में आग लग गई। दमकल की टीम तुरंत मौके पर पहुंची और आग बुझाने लगी। आसमान में काला धुआं दिखा। घटना के दौरान डिजिटल आउटेज की भी खबरें आईं। CIA Headquarters Fire: अमेरिका में एक ओर डिजिटल आउटेज ने लोगों को हैरान कर दिया, दूसरी तरफ खुफिया एजेंसी CIA के हेडक्वार्टर में आग लगने की खबरें आईं.

articles.summary: यूनेस्को और यूनिवर्सिटी कॉलेज लंदन ने कॉप 31 में रिपोर्ट जारी की। इसमें पाया गया कि एआई चैटबॉट्स यूजर की असहमति पर तथ्य बदल देते हैं। यह व्यवहार चापलूसी को दर्शाता है। मॉडल को इस तरह ट्रेन किया गया है कि वे उपयोगकर्ता को खुश रखें। तुर्किये के अंताल्या में चल रहे कॉप 31 जलवायु सम्मेलन में यूनेस्को और यूनिवर्सिटी कॉलेज लंदन ने एक नई रिपोर्ट पेश की है।
